Letter Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n

**New Letters Introduced:**
s, a, t, i, p, n

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n

**Focus:** Mastery of this first, high-utility set of letters and their primary sounds. All lessons and practice problems should ONLY use letters from the Full Practice Set. Students can immediately begin building words like: sat, pat, tap, sip, tip, pin, tin, sit, an, in, it.

Letter Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**New Letters Introduced:**
c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**Focus:** Introduce the new letters while systematically reviewing the letters from Group 1. All lessons and practice problems MUST pull from the full 13-letter cumulative list. A good practice set will have a higher concentration of new letters but will always include review of previous letters.

Letter Group 3: g, o, u, l, f, b

**New Letters Introduced:**
g, o, u, l, f, b

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b

**Focus:** Introduce the new letters while reviewing all 13 previous letters. All lessons and practice problems MUST pull from the full 19-letter cumulative list. Note the intentional separation of 'b' from 'd' (in the previous group) to minimize reversals.

Letter Group 4 (Final): j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**New Letters Introduced:**
j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b, j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**Focus:** Mastery of the full alphabet. All lessons and practice problems MUST pull from the entire 26-letter list. Pedagogical note: The letter 'q' should be taught as the digraph 'qu' as it almost never appears alone in English words.

Letter-Sound Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n

**Focus:** Produce the correct, most common sound for each letter in the set when shown the grapheme (the letter shape). For example, when shown 'a', the student says /ă/ (as in 'apple'). It is crucial to teach clean sounds (e.g., a crisp /t/ sound, not "tuh").

Letter-Sound Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/k/, /ĕ/, /h/, /r/, /m/, /d/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**Focus:** Introduce the new sounds while systematically reviewing the sounds from Group 1. Practice problems must pull from the full 13-letter cumulative list. Note: 'c' and 'k' are introduced together as they make the same primary sound.

Letter-Sound Group 3: g, o, u, l, f, b

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/g/, /ŏ/, /ŭ/, /l/, /f/, /b/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b

**Focus:** Introduce the new sounds while reviewing all 13 previous sounds. Practice problems must pull from the full 19-letter cumulative list.

Letter-Sound Group 4 (Final): j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/j/, /z/, /w/, /v/, /y/, /ks/, /kw/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b, j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**Focus:** Mastery of the sounds for the full alphabet. Note: 'x' makes the /ks/ sound and 'q' is taught as 'qu' making the /kw/ sound.

Letter Formation Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n

**New Letters Introduced:**
s, a, t, i, p, n (uppercase and lowercase)

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n

**Focus:** Correctly forming the letters in this set. Activities should include tracing with guided strokes, and then progress to writing the letters independently. Emphasis is on starting in the right place and following the correct path for each stroke.

Letter Formation Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**New Letters Introduced:**
c, k, e, h, r, m, d (uppercase and lowercase)

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**Focus:** Introduce the formation of the new letters while systematically reviewing the formation of letters from Group 1. Practice must pull from the full 13-letter cumulative list.

Letter Formation Group 3: g, o, u, l, f, b

**New Letters Introduced:**
g, o, u, l, f, b (uppercase and lowercase)

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b

**Focus:** Introduce the formation of the new letters while reviewing all 13 previous letters. Practice must pull from the full 19-letter cumulative list.

Letter Formation Group 4 (Final): j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**New Letters Introduced:**
j, z, w, v, y, x, q (uppercase and lowercase)

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b, j, z, w, v, y, x, q

**Focus:** Mastery of forming all letters of the alphabet correctly.

Decode CVC words with Short 'a' (e.g., cat, map, van)

Focus: Reading CVC words containing the short 'a' sound.
Examples: cat, map, van, sad, tap, bag, ham, pan.

Decode CVC words with Short 'e' (e.g., hen, wet, leg)

Focus: Reading CVC words containing the short 'e' sound.
Examples: hen, wet, leg, bed, pen, men, jet, red.

Decode CVC words with Short 'i' (e.g., pig, sit, fin)
    Focus: Reading CVC words containing the short 'i' sound.
    Examples: pig, sit, fin, big, win, lip, tin, dig.
    Constraints: Generate activities that isolate the short 'i' sound for initial learning. Progress to activities that mix short 'i' words with previously learned short 'a' and 'e' words to test for discrimination (e.g., "pat", "pet", "pit").

Decode CVC words with Short 'o'
    Focus: Reading CVC words containing the short 'o' sound.
    Examples: dog, hot, mop, log, top, pot, hop, fox.
    Constraints: Generate activities that mix short 'o' words with previously learned short 'a', 'e', and 'i' words to ensure discrimination.

Decode CVC words with Short 'u'
    Focus: Reading CVC words containing the short 'u' sound.
    Examples: sun, bug, cup, mud, run, tub, gum, hug.
    Constraints: Generate activities that mix short 'u' words with all four other short vowels to challenge the student's mastery of vowel sounds.

Decode CVC words with Mixed Short Vowels (e.g., cat, hen, pig)
    Focus: This is a summative subskill for CVC decoding. Assess the student's ability to accurately and fluently read CVC words with any of the five short vowel sounds mixed together.
    Task: Present lists of mixed words (e.g., hat, pet, sip, top, mud). Create minimal pair tasks where only the vowel changes (e.g., "Which word is bag? bag, beg, big, bug").

Encode CVC words with Short 'a'

Focus: Spelling CVC words containing the short 'a' sound.
Task: The system should present an audio prompt of a word (e.g., "cat") and the user must type or select the correct letters to spell it.
Examples: cat, map, van, sad, tap, bag.

Encode CVC words with Short 'e'
    Focus: Spelling CVC words with the short 'e' sound when heard aloud.
    Examples: hen, wet, leg, bed, men, red.

Encode CVC words with Short 'i'
    Focus: Spelling CVC words containing the short 'i' sound when heard aloud.
    Task: The system will provide an audio prompt of a word (e.g., "sit") and the user must type or select the correct letters to spell it.
    Examples: sit, pig, fin, big, lip, win.
    Constraints: Only use CVC words with the short 'i' sound. Provide corrective feedback for common errors, such as vowel confusion (e.g., spelling 'set' instead of 'sit').

Encode CVC words with Short 'o'
    Focus: Spelling CVC words with the short 'o' sound when heard aloud.
    Examples: dog, hot, mop, log, top.

Encode CVC words with Short 'u'
    Focus: Spelling CVC words with the short 'u' sound when heard aloud.
    Examples: sun, bug, cup, mud, run.

skill:
Application of CVC Word Knowledge
This skill consolidates learning by asking students to use their CVC word knowledge in more complex tasks like reading sentences, building fluency, and checking for comprehension.
text:
Discriminate between Real & Nonsense CVC Words
Focus: To assess pure decoding skills by having the student apply phonics rules to both real and phonetically plausible nonsense words. This confirms they understand the CVC pattern, not just memorized a list of words.

Task: Present the student with a pair of CVC words: one real word and one nonsense word. The student must read both and select the real word.

Examples:

    "Which is a real word? map or mep"

    "Find the real word: fin or fip"

    Constraints & Scaffolding:

        Nonsense words must be phonetically plausible and follow the CVC pattern (e.g., zot, keg, sib). Avoid unpronounceable combinations (e.g., qbc).

        Initially, use nonsense words that are very different from the real word.

        Increase difficulty by using minimal pairs where only one letter is different (especially the vowel), forcing careful decoding (e.g., cat vs. cot).

skill:
Application of CVC Word Knowledge
This skill consolidates learning by asking students to use their CVC word knowledge in more complex tasks like reading sentences, building fluency, and checking for comprehension.
text:
Read CVC Words in Decodable Phrases & Sentences

    Focus: To transition the student from decoding isolated words to reading connected text for meaning. This builds foundational reading comprehension and syntax awareness.

    Task: Generate short, highly controlled phrases and sentences for the student to read aloud. The system can then ask a simple comprehension question.

    Examples:

        Phrases: "a red bug", "the big pig", "on top", "a wet cat"

        Sentences: "The cat sat on the mat.", "A bug is in the cup.", "Did the dog run?"

    Constraints & Scaffolding:

        Strictly use only mastered CVC words and a small, pre-defined set of high-frequency sight words (e.g., a, the, is, on, in, did, see). Do NOT introduce any words that are not decodable or on the sight word list.

        Begin with 3-word phrases.

        Progress to 4-5 word declarative sentences.

        Finally, introduce simple questions ending in a question mark.

skill:
Application of CVC Word Knowledge
This skill consolidates learning by asking students to use their CVC word knowledge in more complex tasks like reading sentences, building fluency, and checking for comprehension.
text:
Build Fluency with CVC Word Lists & Chains

    Focus: To increase the speed and automaticity of CVC word recognition. The goal is for the student to read the words accurately and quickly, without needing to sound them out laboriously each time.

    Task: Generate two types of activities:

        Word Lists: A list of 5-10 mastered CVC words for timed reading.

        Word Chains/Ladders: A sequence of words where only one letter changes from one word to the next. The student reads down the chain.

    Examples:

        Word List: [ cat, sun, pig, hot, bed, man, leg, cup ]

        Word Chain: cat -> mat -> man -> pan -> pin -> fin

    Constraints & Scaffolding:

        Word lists should be a random mix of all mastered short vowels.

        Word chains must follow the one-letter-change rule. They can change the initial, medial, or final sound.

        These activities are often timed (e.g., "How many words can you read in one minute?"), which the UI should support.

text:
Match CVC Words to Pictures

    Focus: To ensure the student is reading for meaning by connecting a decoded word to its visual representation. This is a direct check for comprehension and vocabulary.

    Task: Present the student with a single CVC word and a set of 2-4 images. The student must select the image that matches the word.

    Examples:

        Target Word: sun

        Image Choices: [ a picture of a sun ], [ a picture of a bug ], [ a picture of a cat ]

    Constraints & Scaffolding:

        The distractor images are very important. They should represent other CVC words that the student has learned.

        To increase difficulty, make the distractor words phonetically similar to the target word. For the target pin, use images for pen and pan as distractors. This forces the student to pay close attention to the vowel sound.
